name: MonarchInlineCodeStyle
title: InlineCode
wrapsNative: AttributedString runs (inlinePresentationIntent .code, SwiftUI foregroundColor and backgroundColor attributes) drawn by Text
summary: The look of a code fragment inside running text, as attributes of an AttributedString run: the monospaced face at the size of the surrounding text, on a muted background (subtle) or without one (plain).
whenToUse: For a function name, a path, a command or a value to type inside a sentence. Use markdown(_:in:textStyle:) for text with backticks, attributedString(_:in:textStyle:) for a single fragment.
whenNotToUse: Not for a block of code or anything longer than a few words; set that as its own Text with the code role of monarchTextStyle. Not for keyboard shortcuts; use MonarchKbd.
api: func attributes(in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributeContainer
func attributedString(_ code: String, in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributedString
func applied(to text: AttributedString, in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributedString
func markdown(_ markdown: String, in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributedString

options.name: variant
options.description: subtle draws a muted background behind the code; plain only switches to the monospaced face.

options.name: theme
options.description: The theme from the environment. An attributed string holds colours, not roles, so the theme is passed in.

options.name: textStyle
options.description: The type role of the surrounding text. Used only when the theme has its own code font family, to size that font.

appearance: The code is in the default text colour and the monospaced face. Subtle adds the muted background colour of the theme behind the characters; plain adds nothing. The colours are those of the theme passed in, so the text is rebuilt when the theme changes.
platformNotes: The web InlineCode is an element; on iOS running text is one Text, so the style produces AttributedString runs instead of a view. Text draws the background flush with the characters: the padding and the rounded corners of the web chip are not available, and the code is the size of the surrounding text, not 0.9 of it. The web nowrap option is not offered; a long token breaks where it does not fit. Android covers this with a text style in MonarchTypography.
accessibility: The code run is part of the Text and is read by VoiceOver in place, as its characters.
Code differs from the text around it by the monospaced face, so it is recognisable without the background colour, including in the plain variant.
With the system font the run follows the size of the surrounding text at every Dynamic Type size. A custom code font family is sized from the given role and scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: The attributed string holds resolved colours. Build it in the view body from the environment's theme so that it follows light, dark and high contrast.
markdown(_:in:textStyle:) reads inline Markdown only and keeps white space. An unmatched backtick is shown as it is. Text that cannot be parsed is shown unchanged.
applied(to:in:textStyle:) styles only runs whose inline presentation intent contains code and keeps their other attributes.
A long token such as a hash wraps by character where it does not fit a line.

examples.title: In a sentence
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading) {
    Text(MonarchInlineCodeStyle.subtle.markdown("Set `timeout` to a number of seconds, then run `npm run sync`.", in: theme))
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
    Text(MonarchInlineCodeStyle.subtle.markdown("The file is saved to `exports/2026/report.csv`.", in: theme))
        .monarchTextStyle(.caption)
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textMuted)
}
